text: Every record on Propchain is attested.
But attestation proves provenance, not truth. A rent roll full of phantom tenants can be perfectly signed, and perfectly false.
And consensus can't decide whether a tenant exists.
Most fraud loss is misstated income, or diverted closing funds. Both have a truth the platform can see: cash.
The aim is to make lies expensive, and detectable.
The defence is six layers, each stopping what the one below cannot: identity, provenance, corroboration, bonds, professional signatures, and memory.
What gets through all six is what insurance prices.
Corroboration first. One asset's annual rent, from four sources.
The rent roll says one million and twenty thousand euros. The manager's ledger agrees, but it follows the seller: one source, not two.
Bank receipts show nine hundred and fifty-eight thousand. Tenants confirm nine fifty-five.
Cash outranks documents. The quorum settles at nine fifty-six, and the field reaches level A three: reconciled to cash.
Counterparties can require a level, field by field, from A zero to A five. And A four needs something new: capital at risk.
A bond is a holdback with rules instead of lawyers. An illustrative deal: thirteen million euros, eight hundred thousand of attested income, a six point one five percent cap rate.
The seller warrants that income within five percent, for twelve months. A forty-thousand tolerance.
The bond covers the buyer's loss at a ten percent miss: eighty thousand over the cap rate. One point three million, held in a yield-bearing escrow.
Twelve months of bank receipts decide.
Income of seven sixty is a five percent miss, inside tolerance. The bond is released in full.
At seven twenty, the miss is five points beyond tolerance. Half the bond goes to the buyer. Pro rata, never all or nothing.
That only works where a later truth exists, that a contract can read.
Rent against receipts. Title against the registry. Bondable.
Building condition? Only with a referee, named in advance.
Valuations and opinions: never.
Staking learned this. Slashing works on facts the chain can see, and has failed wherever disputed conduct was put to a vote.
So who posts the capital? Usually, it isn't new money. The bond replaces the holdback, or W and I premium, a sale already carries.
The seller can self-bond. A surety can post for a fee. Or the buyer can hold a policy, on the same trigger.
The market is the middle one: sureties quoting on the same attested record, with fees that fall with level and track record.
Sellers bond only if certainty, a higher rank, firm debt, speed, is worth more than the cost. That has to be measured, not assumed.
And the native insurer? There are three paths.
As for a native insurer: a data partner needs no capital. An M G A underwrites on a carrier's capital. An own carrier needs a licence, and solvency capital. The realistic route is A, then B.
The edge is observation. The platform sees what was claimed at close, and what was realised for years after. That pairing is a loss curve no incumbent has.
So short-tail, parametric cover comes first, because it teaches fastest. Float comes last.
It's a working draft, and the numbers are illustrative. But the plan is simple.
Measure first. Bond what is measured. Insure the rest.
